Exposure & Risk

The demand case runs through reactor life extensions and new builds, with fuel bought years ahead, so contract prices move slowly but persistently. Exposure runs through Cameco and URA, while enrichment via Centrus, down 2.19% over five sessions, carries more policy risk. Lists such as Yahoo Finance's best nuclear energy stocks [[n0648]] show the theme is drawing a wider audience.
Trigger to Watch

A URA close that erases its 1.33% five-session gain would signal fatigue; a fresh round of utility term contracting, or a strong close in Cameco while URA holds its 20-session gain, would extend the move.

underowned.title: The Korea discount
parts: Attention Gap

CNBC asks whether the Korea discount makes the market a value stock or a value trap [[n0734]]. The KOSPI closed at 2,495.66, up 8.01% over 20 sessions, and SK Hynix at 130,700 KRW is up 9.74% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Exposure & Risk

Memory is the earnings engine, and memory pricing turns faster than logic, so Korean earnings revisions can swing sharply. Small investors are joining the dispute over a politically motivated ban on short selling [[n1485]], a liquidity distortion that can reverse if the ban is lifted and may flatter recent gains.
Trigger to Watch

Samsung Electronics, at 71,300 KRW and down 1.93% over five sessions, regaining momentum alongside memory pricing would validate the discount closing; a policy U-turn on shorting would test how much of the rally was mechanical.

underowned.title: Medical devices after the GLP-1 scare
parts: Attention Gap

Moomoo argues the medical-device selloff caused by Ozempic fears has gone too far and that the stocks are rebounding [[n0321]]. Intuitive Surgical closed at 314.98 USD, up 21.62% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27), while the GLP-1 headlines keep the spotlight on the drugmakers themselves.
Exposure & Risk

The selloff priced fewer procedures well before any measurable effect on volumes. The risk is that each new efficacy datapoint, such as the analysis showing Lilly's Mounjaro beating Novo's drug [[n1623]], revives the fewer-procedures narrative before volumes can disprove it. Exposure is best held through diversified large-cap device makers rather than single-procedure specialists.
Trigger to Watch
Procedure-volume commentary in the next company updates; Intuitive Surgical holding its 3.18% five-session gain would show buyers absorbing GLP-1 headlines.

underowned.title: Gold miners versus bullion
parts: Attention Gap

Gold has gone nowhere, at 2,012.40 USD/oz and up only 0.34% over 20 sessions, yet GDX gained 4.78% over five sessions and Newmont 5.03% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). The Northern Miner expects gold and silver to rise as political and economic risks grind on [[n0129]].
Exposure & Risk

Miners amplify bullion both ways: Reuters reported gold dropping below $2,000 as the dollar gained and yields pared losses [[n1720]], and that is the downside path if US data re-accelerate. Fixed costs mean a small bullion gain becomes a large margin gain, but cost inflation can absorb it.
Trigger to Watch
DXY breaking below 103.20 with falling real yields would confirm the setup; a gold close back below the 20-session reference while miners hold would signal crowding.

crypto.title: Bitcoin consolidates as ETF anticipation meets the Binance clean-up
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at 37,254.17 USD, down 0.60% on the day and 0.48% over five days but up 5.11% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2023-11-27). Ether closed at 2,027.42 USD after a 1.74% drop, Solana gave back 4.47% to 55.06 USD after a 27.78% 20-day surge, and XRP is down 11.98% over 20 days. Reuters had bitcoin rising 5.7% to $37,802 [[n0769]] in the same week as the Binance charges, and it has since drifted back below that level. Dispersion inside crypto is widening: speculative flows chase smaller ecosystems while bitcoin consolidates in a range. Ether's 7.38% 20-day gain trails Solana by a wide margin, which suggests rotation within the asset class rather than fresh money entering it.
New / Most Important

Market structure is improving even as the largest exchange is penalised. Fortune reports Binance's BNB token dropped on criminal charges while bitcoin dipped only slightly [[n0761]], a sign that the market reads an enforced clean-up as reducing tail risk rather than adding it. The more important signal is GBTC's discount to NAV falling below 10% for the first time in two years [[n0779]]: a narrowing discount suggests the market is increasingly pricing a conversion to a spot ETF. Coinbase rose to its highest since May 2022 [[n0559]], and COIN is up 69.21% over 20 sessions, including a 3.66% gain in the last session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Playbook

Hold core bitcoin, but do not lever the ETF story through proxies that already discount it: COIN gained 20.92% and Marathon 12.80% over five sessions. Trigger to add: bitcoin reclaiming the $37,802 level Reuters reported [[n0769]] on a daily close. What changes the call: tighter retail rules spreading beyond Singapore, where the MAS will bar retail customers from buying crypto with local credit cards [[n1484]], or a regulatory delay that sends proxies down faster than the coin. Position sizing should assume the ETF decision is binary for the proxies and only incremental for bitcoin itself.

flows.title: Liquidity loosens as the dollar heads for its worst month of 2023
parts: Global Liquidity

Financial conditions eased sharply over the month. Business Insider says the dollar is on pace for its worst month of 2023 on bets the Fed is done raising rates [[n1789]]; DXY closed at 103.20, down 3.15% over 20 sessions, and the dollar-denominated EM bond ETF EMB is up 5.38% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). The Financial Times says emerging-market central banks may be trumping the Fed and ECB [[n0981]]. The counterweight is supply: $7.6 trillion of US government debt matures in the next year [[n0135]]. Easier conditions are being financed through a heavy refinancing calendar, which is why term premium is the variable to watch. For now the transmission is textbook: lower US yields weaken the dollar, a weaker dollar eases dollar-debt burdens in emerging markets, and that can let EM central banks ease without defending their currencies.
Rates & Dollar

The rates leg is a bull flattener, with the 10Y at 4.39% and the 2Y at 4.84% (US Treasury, prior close 2023-11-27). TLT jumped 1.67% in the last session and 8.21% over 20 sessions, while SHY rose only 0.37% over 20 and IEF 3.21%, the steadier way to own the move with less convexity risk than TLT (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Reuters says the dollar is weakening as the Fed rate-cut view weighs [[n0098]], and BofA Global Research calls 2024 the year of the landing [[n0665]]. Gold, at 2,012.40 USD/oz, has barely responded to the softer dollar, a sign that real-rate relief is being expressed in equities and bonds rather than in hard assets. The dollar's slide is mostly a rates story; it would end quickly if US data re-accelerated while Europe stagnates.
Credit Check

High yield has joined the rally: HYG is up 3.80% over 20 sessions and LQD 5.98%. Beneath the surface the cycle is turning. Economists cited by Business Insider say a default cycle has started amid the Fed's high rates [[n1050]], and the ECB warns eurozone banks are showing stress as loan defaults rise [[n0986]]. China's shadow-bank shortfall [[n0209]] is the emerging-market version of the same problem. Tight spreads plus rising defaults is a late-cycle combination that favours investment grade over high yield, because the rally in junk has priced lower rates but not higher losses. The tell would be HYG lagging LQD on a day Treasuries rally, the point where credit stops trading as duration and starts trading as default risk.
Equity & Fund Flows

Cash is still on the sidelines. Wolf Street reports money market funds, large CDs and small CDs all surged [[n1042]], and Business Insider argues a FOMO rally could hit stocks after investors sold [[n1046]]. That cash is the fuel for a year-end chase if yields keep falling, because money-fund yields reset lower with policy expectations. Positioning is already crowded in places, with Goldman saying hedge-fund bets on US stocks are the most crowded ever [[n0303]], and speculative wrappers are running hot, with ARKK up 33.28% over 20 sessions and the 3x Nasdaq 100 ETF TQQQ up 40.73%. The mix is retail-and-cash support underneath, crowded professional positioning on top. Outside the US, VGK is up 11.42% over 20 sessions in dollar terms, so part of the non-US equity return for dollar-based investors has come from the weaker dollar rather than from earnings.
Portfolio Implication

Rotate rather than add gross exposure. Own duration through IEF and quality growth, funded by energy and European autos; keep EM bonds via EMB while the dollar softens; and use the cheap VIX at 12.69 to hedge. Trigger to extend risk: money-market cash rotating into equity funds while DXY holds below 103.20. What changes the call: DXY reclaiming its 20-session-ago level of 106.56, or a jump in high-yield defaults that pulls HYG below its prior close of 75.11 USD, either of which would mean the liquidity impulse is reversing. Until then, the asymmetry favours owning what benefits from lower rates without needing stronger growth: duration, quality software, regulated utilities and data-centre real estate.

anticipatory.title: OPEC+ after the delay: a cut the market is not paying for
parts: What Is Priced

WTI at 74.86 USD/bbl is down 12.49% over 20 sessions and Brent 8.54% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). CNN reports oil dropped 4% on the OPEC meeting delay [[n1541]]. Brent's 2.84% five-session decline into the meeting shows sellers still in control. The market is pricing disagreement inside the group, not a deeper cut, and energy equities have been used as a funding short against the duration rally.
Conditional Expression

If the delayed meeting delivers deeper or extended cuts, the cleanest expression is long XLE and ConocoPhillips, down 2.55% over 20 sessions, against airlines and gasoline-sensitive retailers. If it ends in quota disputes, extend the consumer leg and add to duration as the oil-driven inflation-expectations channel cools further.
Risk

Producers sound combative, with OPEC's head accusing the IEA of vilifying the industry [[n1626]], while Venezuela says it is producing 850,000 bpd and wants to regain US market share [[n0884]]. A WTI close back above its 20-session-ago level of 85.54 would mean the market under-priced cohesion; a break below 74.86 would mean the cut disappointed.

anticipatory.title: Fed cuts in 2024: priced before the data confirm them
parts: What Is Priced

Bank of America says rate cuts are coming next year [[n1786]], and the curve agrees: the 2Y at 4.84% sits well below the 3M bill at 5.49% (US Treasury, prior close 2023-11-27). VIX at 12.69 shows equity investors treating the landing as soft, and a dollar weakening on the rate-cut view [[n0098]] carries the same assumption into currencies.
Conditional Expression

If the next payroll and inflation prints extend the cooling seen in October, when unemployment rose to 3.9% [[n1664]], add to 2Y Treasuries and rate-sensitive equities such as XLRE. If services inflation re-accelerates, the 2Y is the most exposed point on the curve because it has priced the most relief.
Risk

The latest Fed minutes show a consensus that rates need to stay high [[n0294]], so officials can push back verbally before any data turn. A 2Y move back to the 4.99% of 20 observations ago would unwind a month of easing in one step and hit the most crowded equity longs first.

anticipatory.title: Spot bitcoin ETF: the discount is already closing
parts: What Is Priced

GBTC's discount to NAV has fallen below 10% for the first time in two years [[n0779]], and Coinbase stock has reached its highest since May 2022 [[n0559]]. COIN is up 69.21% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27), so equity proxies already discount a favourable regulatory outcome.
Conditional Expression

If approval comes, the remaining upside sits in GBTC's residual discount and in bitcoin itself rather than in proxies that have already run. If a decision is deferred, expect proxies such as Riot, up 12.79% over five sessions, to fall faster than bitcoin, so a long-bitcoin, short-miner pair is the cleaner way to hold the view.
Risk

Enforcement is the other side of legitimacy: Binance's BNB token dropped on criminal charges [[n0761]], and regulators can attach conditions that slow inflows. A bitcoin close below its five-day reference would show the ETF bid fading before any decision, and MicroStrategy's 4.78% drop in the last session shows how fast leveraged proxies give back gains.

anticipatory.title: China developer lending: from weighing to funding
parts: What Is Priced

The Business Times reports Beijing weighing first-ever unsecured loans to builders [[n0208]], yet the Hang Seng at 17,525.06 is up only 0.68% over 20 sessions and FXI 1.36% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Markets are pricing talk, not money, and the Shanghai Composite's 1.19% five-session decline shows onshore investors waiting for allocations rather than announcements.
Conditional Expression

If a programme is confirmed with named banks and sizes, buy Hong Kong-listed China exposure via FXI and copper miners such as Freeport, with BHP as the lower-beta version. If the measure stays at the consideration stage, fade rallies in China beta and keep exposure in quality platforms such as Tencent.
Risk

Profit growth is slowing [[n0224]] and a shadow-bank shortfall [[n0209]] shows losses are still being recognised, so support can arrive and still be swamped by falling household confidence. A Shanghai Composite close below 3,031.70 alongside a weaker yuan would mean policy is losing the race.

catalysts.title: Nvidia (NVDA): record quarter meets a China delay
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Nvidia reported record revenue and earnings for its fiscal third quarter [[n0848]], yet shares closed down on a report it delayed a China AI chip designed to comply with US export rules [[n0218]]. Thesis: AI data-centre demand outweighs the China leakage, because the delayed product serves a market that export rules already cap.
Price Hurdle & Risk

NVDA closed at 482.42 USD, up 0.98% in the last session, down 2.14% over five and up 19.12% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Risk: a second China setback or a broader AI multiple reset.

Accumulate on closes above 482.42 USD; pair against a semiconductor ETF to isolate execution from sector beta. Exit if the five-session loss deepens while SOXX holds, a sign the market is pricing company-specific China risk.

catalysts.title: Volkswagen (VOW3.DE): restructuring a brand that is 'no longer competitive'
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Reuters reports Volkswagen will reduce headcount at its core brand, which management calls no longer competitive [[n0747]]. Thesis: savings take years, while the cost gap with Chinese EV makers is widening now, and headcount cuts in Germany are slow and expensive.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The preference shares closed at 106.12 EUR, down 0.82% in the last session and 2.50% over five, though still up 7.04% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Risk: an aggressive cost target that the market rewards early, as it often does with restructurings.
Trade Expression

Underweight against the STOXX autos tracker. Add if the shares close below 106.12 EUR with the five-session decline extending; cover on evidence of cuts beyond headcount, such as plant capacity, or a sector-wide relief rally led by China-exposed peers.

catalysts.title: Deere (DE): guidance miss meets a right-to-repair ruling
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Agriculture Dive says Deere is bracing for a sharp drop in tractor demand despite a profitable year [[n0678]], and Reuters reports a judge ruled Deere must face US farmers' right-to-repair lawsuits [[n0679]], a threat to high-margin parts and service revenue that cushions equipment downturns.
Price Hurdle & Risk

DE closed at 362.21 USD, down 2.16% in the last session and 5.71% over five, almost flat over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Risk: farm income surprises or buybacks cushioning the downturn.
Trade Expression

Stay underweight while the stock trades below 362.21 USD and the five-session trend stays negative. Cover if Caterpillar, down 2.24% over five sessions, and Deere stabilise together, which would signal the capex downturn is priced. Until then, rallies in agricultural machinery are selling opportunities.

catalysts.title: Eli Lilly (LLY): head-to-head data favours Mounjaro
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Reuters reports a data analysis finding Mounjaro led to more and faster weight loss than Novo's obesity drug [[n1623]], and Bloomberg expects Zepbound to be another hit [[n1624]]. Thesis: efficacy leadership plus a fresh launch converts into share gains against Novo in a supply-constrained market.
Price Hurdle & Risk
LLY closed at 591.53 USD, down 1.59% in the last session and up 5.59% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Risk: supply constraints that cap volumes, and pricing pressure from Washington.
Trade Expression

Buy weakness toward the prior close and hold Lilly against Novo Nordisk's US line, which is up 11.09% over 20 sessions. Reassess if Novo's capacity additions close the supply gap faster than Lilly's, since in a supply-limited market capacity decides share.

catalysts.title: Marvell (MRVL): AI networking has to beat a raised bar
parts: Catalyst & Thesis
Yahoo Finance expects Marvell to beat earnings estimates [[n0123]]. The thesis is that AI networking demand can carry the quarter, but with the stock up 18.28% over 20 sessions the bar has risen.
Price Hurdle & Risk

MRVL closed at 55.90 USD, down 0.23% in the last session, up 0.58% over five and up 18.28% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Risk: a beat without a raised AI outlook, which a stock that has already rallied can sell off on.
Trade Expression

Express through options rather than stock: own upside only if guidance lifts AI revenue expectations. A close above 55.90 USD after results with a positive five-session change confirms; a drop below 47.26 USD, the level of 20 sessions ago, would reverse the month's gains and signal that the AI premium is narrowing to Nvidia alone.

catalysts.title: Alibaba (BABA): a founder's reversal and a sliding stock
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

CNN reports Jack Ma backed off plans to sell Alibaba shares after the stock plunged [[n0517]], and is betting on a new food business in China [[n0241]]. Thesis: the founder stepping back from a sale removes an overhang, but his attention moving to a food venture and a 6.39% 20-session slide leave investors without a clear catalyst.
Price Hurdle & Risk

BABA closed at 77.53 USD, down 1.22% in the last session and 6.39% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Risk: Beijing's market-support measures lift large caps indiscriminately and squeeze shorts.
Trade Expression

Underweight Alibaba against Tencent within China internet exposure, a pair that isolates execution from policy. Cover if BABA reclaims its 20-session-ago level of 82.82 USD or if a buyback acceleration is announced.

spec.retail_intro: The dominant popular narrative is the Cybertruck halo: Tesla's believers expect one outrageous truck to recharge the brand and the stock at once, the halo-product mechanism in which a flagship few will buy sells the rest, while Affirm rode the online shopping record, Lilly won a weight-loss head-to-head and index buyers chased a cooling streak.

retail.title: Tesla / TSLA — The Cybertruck lands, believers want a halo
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Tesla's believers have waited a long time for this truck, and it is finally here. Barron's says the Cybertruck has arrived and investors hope for a halo effect [[n0738]], and The Conversation argues the company's success is riding on it [[n1632]]. Tesla closed at 236.08 USD, up 0.27% on the day and 13.88% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). The story retail tells itself is that a single outrageous product can relight the brand and the share price together, and that the critics who mocked the stainless-steel wedge are about to be proven wrong again. The emotional hook is vindication: owning Tesla has always been a bet on Musk making the impossible ship.
What Is Driving It

The catalyst is the delivery event. Business Insider reports an executive saying Tesla will deliver only 10 Cybertrucks at its big event this month [[n0853]], so the moment is symbolic before it is financial. The first impressions are glowing: InsideEVs says its reporter saw the truck up close and is still picking a jaw off the floor [[n1620]], and the Autopian says a production-spec Cybertruck looks good [[n1604]]. The competitive backdrop is harsher. El País says BYD is going after Tesla's throne with more than 300,000 electric cars sold in a month [[n0275]], and Reuters says Volkswagen will cut headcount at a VW brand it calls no longer competitive [[n0747]]. Among US EV names, Rivian rose 1.40% while NIO fell 2.84% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
The Social Signal

The attention is unmistakable even without a price surge. The Autopian posted a bunch of photos of a production-spec truck so readers can judge for themselves [[n1604]] and even interviewed the people who brought a Cybertruck clone to a major car show [[n1549]], and TechCrunch reports a virtual garage sale that lets you haggle with AIs to buy Tesla stock [[n0742]]. Barchart is asking whether Tesla can really sell 20 million cars by 2030 [[n0356]], the kind of long-range number believers repeat. A stock that is only up 0.76% over five sessions while the coverage piles up (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27) suggests the crowd is waiting for the event to supply the next leg rather than buying ahead of it.
Historical Analog

The mechanism is the halo product, the one Barron's names directly [[n0738]]. A flagship that few people will buy can still lift the brand, pull showroom traffic and remind customers why they chose the company, but its own sales rarely move earnings early on. That makes halo launches reflexive for the stock: the excitement is priced on the day the product is shown, while the numbers that prove or disprove the halo arrive quarters later. It also explains why a launch can be a sell-the-news event even when the product is a hit: the buyers who wanted exposure to the spectacle already own it. With only a handful of trucks due at the event [[n0853]], the gap between spectacle and volume is the whole trade.
Smart Money View

The bulls point to dominance at home: BloombergNEF says Tesla's grip on the US looks secure with rivals many rungs down [[n0854]], and Forbes explains why Tesla dominates with the Model Y plus the plug [[n1610]]. The skeptics point to valuation and margins. Forbes reports Bernstein saying the $649 billion valuation gap between Tesla and BYD is unjustified [[n0733]], and Barron's says Tesla has new deals on its Model Y that investors might not love [[n0466]], because discounts eat margin. The WSJ adds that Musk's social-media comments have sparked a Tesla investor backlash [[n1474]]. The split is about whether a halo can offset price cuts.
When the Narrative Breaks

The first trigger is quality. Business Insider says the Cybertruck's stainless-steel body is reportedly leading to gaps between the panels [[n0941]]; if early owners turn panel gaps into viral clips, the halo inverts. The second is the ramp: a symbolic handover of a handful of trucks [[n0853]] invites the question of when volume arrives, and a vague answer would hand the stage back to BYD [[n0275]]. The third is price. Tesla's 207.30 USD close 20 sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27) marks where the 20-session run began; a sell-the-news slide toward it would say the event was the top. More Model Y discounting [[n0466]] would hit the margin story at the same time.

retail.title: Affirm / AFRM — Splitting the bill on a record weekend
parts: Why Retail Is Here

On Cyber Monday, the button that splits the bill got its own rally. Affirm jumped 11.97% to 29.37 USD and is up 73.48% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27), a move that lands after CNBC reported a record $9.8 billion Black Friday online spend, up 7.5% [[n0132]]. Yahoo Finance's guide to the top buy now, pay later apps of 2023 [[n0470]] shows how mainstream the habit has become. The crowd's logic: every online record is volume for the lender sitting inside the checkout.
Where It Breaks

Pay-later lending thrives when shoppers are stretched, which is also its risk: the NYT says there is a lot riding on Black Friday and Cyber Monday [[n0153]], and a season financed in instalments shows its cost only when the bills come due. Funding is the other lever. The 10Y yield is 4.39%, down 45 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2023-11-27), and Reuters says the dollar weakened as the Fed rate-cut view weighed [[n0098]]; if that view reverses, a lender priced like a growth stock reprices fast. A 73.48% run in 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27) can unwind in days.

retail.title: Eli Lilly / LLY — Mounjaro wins the head-to-head, stock shrugs
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The weight-loss crowd got the head-to-head it wanted. Reuters says Lilly's Mounjaro led to more and faster weight loss than Novo's obesity drug in a data analysis [[n1623]], and CNBC says the real-world study found Mounjaro more effective than Ozempic for overweight and obese adults [[n0718]]. Yahoo Finance reports Jim Cramer is adamant that analysts are insane to be so wary of revolutionary weight-loss drugs [[n0753]], the kind of television conviction that tends to keep retail buying. Yet Lilly fell 1.59% to 591.53 USD, though it remains up 5.59% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27).
Where It Breaks

Beating Novo is not the same as beating expectations: Novo itself slipped only 0.93% to 710.00 DKK (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27), so investors are pricing two winners, not one. Fierce Pharma says Novo keeps its GLP-1 expansion spree rolling with a $2.3B manufacturing upgrade in France [[n0934]], and Business Insider says a $1.7 billion digital-health upstart is sitting out the Ozempic craze for now [[n0751]]. Supply catching up erodes the shortage premium, and a slide toward 560.23 USD, Lilly's close 20 sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27), would say the data was already priced.

retail.title: S&P 500 ETF / SPY — Chasing a cooling streak into year-end
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Investors who missed November's rally may want in before the year closes, the FOMO scenario Business Insider describes [[n1046]]. The Los Angeles Times says Wall Street edged lower as a four-week winning streak cooled off [[n0155]], but SPY still sits at 454.48 USD, up 10.67% over 20 sessions, with the VIX at 12.69 points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27). Investing.com says Bank of America technical analysts see much more upside for US indices and ETFs [[n0265]], and BofA Global Research calls 2024 the year of the landing [[n0665]]. The fuel is rates: the 10Y yield is 4.39%, down 45 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2023-11-27).
Where It Breaks

A cooling streak is where late buyers get tested. Bloomberg says global central bankers are warning of uncertainty amid the rate debate [[n0151]], and AllianceBernstein asks whether equity risk is worth the reward in a world of higher bond yields [[n0240]]. With the VIX down 40.34% over 20 sessions, insurance is cheap; a jump back toward 21.27 points, its level 20 sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-27), would turn year-end FOMO into a scramble, and 410.68 USD marks where SPY's run began.
